name: West Arete
approach: Start at the Eldorado Creek trailhead on Cascade River Road, follow the climbers' trail up Eldorado Creek into the Roush Creek basin, traverse below the Eldorado Glacier to the notch between Eldorado and The Triad, descend the glacier on the notch's northwest side, then traverse beneath the West Face rock ribs to reach the arete. Typically a 3-day trip (approach day, climb day, exit day); the first roughly 800 ft of climbing is Class 4 before harder 5th-class sections.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Creek Trailhead (Cascade River Road)
waypoints.note: Same Cascade River Road trailhead as the standard route; the route follows the standard climbers' trail from the North Fork Cascade River up Eldorado Creek and into the Roush Creek basin before diverging west toward the Eldorado/Triad notch and West Face.
waypoints.directions: From SR-20 at Marblemount, cross the Skagit River onto Cascade River Road and drive about 20 miles (pavement gives way to gravel around mile 10) to the parking area at about 2,100 ft near Eldorado Creek. Overnight stays in North Cascades National Park need a backcountry permit. The road is often not open this far until late June.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Peak
waypoints.directions: Cross the Cascade River on logs a short way downstream of the parking and follow the steep climbers' trail up beside Eldorado Creek into the Roush Creek basin and onto the Eldorado Glacier. From the glacier, descend west into the Marble Creek cirque to the toe of the arete near 6,000 ft, then climb the arete, about 2,800 ft of loose 4th class to 5.8 on and near the crest, to the summit.
